what: Expeditors International arranges freight. It books space on ships and aircraft, handles customs clearance and manages supply chains for importers and exporters, but owns no ships or planes of its own.
customers: Manufacturers, retailers and distributors moving goods internationally, especially between Asia and North America.
moat: An asset-light model that earns a spread on freight whichever way rates move, run by a company whose staff are paid from branch profit rather than volume.
risks: Freight rates collapsed from pandemic highs, and revenue fell about 13% a year over three years
Tariffs and trade disruption change shipping patterns unpredictably
It has no long-term contracts with customers
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 27% with cash exceeding debt
Revenue grew about 4% last year as volumes stabilised
Owning no assets means it stays profitable even in the worst freight markets
watch: Airfreight and ocean tonnage volumes and net revenue per shipment.
